# CRLF Line Endings Breaking Bash Scripts Under WSL

Discovered while debugging a CrashLoopBackOff caused by a script edited on
Windows and executed in a Linux container, 2026-06.

## Behavior

A shell script with CRLF line endings fails under bash. The `\r` is parsed as
part of the token, so:

```sh
set -euo pipefail
```

becomes `set -euo pipefail\r`, and bash produces:

```text
set: pipefail: invalid option name
```

The script exits non-zero (or, for a container entrypoint, produces a
CrashLoopBackOff at exit 2). Every line is affected similarly — the trailing
`\r` corrupts variable names, shebang lines, and any other token that contains
it.

## Cause

Editors on Windows (notably VS Code) save files with CRLF by default. A script
originally written with LF line endings silently picks up CRLF if it is opened
and saved in VS Code without a per-repo `.gitattributes` or editor override.
The corruption is not visible in the editor and the file appears correct on
inspection with `cat` (which hides `\r`).

## Detection

```sh
file <script>   # reports "with CRLF line terminators" if affected
```

`xxd` or `od -c` also show `\r\n` pairs at line ends.

## Remedy (one-off)

```sh
sed -i 's/\r//' <script>
# or
dos2unix <script>
```

## Prevention (durable)

A `.gitattributes` rule in the repository pins shell scripts and Makefiles to
LF regardless of the editor or OS:

```gitattributes
*.sh        eol=lf
*.mk        eol=lf
Makefile    eol=lf
```

The prescriptive rule for this (what to put in `.gitattributes` and where)
lives in [jewzaam/standards](https://github.com/jewzaam/standards).
